network.overall_strategy: Prioritize the strongest Arg-specific evidence. The backbone is a surficial cyanosulfidic network because Patel et al. (2015) provide the clearest de novo route from simple feedstocks to the experimentally characterized arginine alpha-aminonitrile; Cu-assisted and Cu-free photoredox variants are represented separately, and free arginine is reached by lower-confidence hydrolysis of that precursor. A secondary Orn-first module is retained because Orn-to-Arg guanidination is chemically strong, but its ornithine-supply step is explicitly marked speculative and connected to the shared C3 aldehyde rather than to contested direct Fischer-Tropsch-type Arg claims or the still-incomplete H2/Ni glutamate branch.

reactions.name: Cu(I)-mediated coupling of hydrogen cyanide and acetylene to acrylonitrile

conditions.other: Anoxic shallow aqueous pool or stream margin; staged cyanide availability; evaporative concentration plausible

reactions.mechanism: Copper-mediated C-C coupling of cyanide-derived carbon with acetylene yields the C3 vinyl nitrile entry node.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) identify HCN plus acetylene as the entry to the arginine/proline C3 nitrile branch via copper-mediated chemistry. A surface aqueous setting is favored because the demonstrated network is surficial rather than submarine, and cyanide concentration is better justified in closed-basin lake or pool settings than in the deep ocean (Patel et al., 2015; Toner and Catling, 2019; Ranjan and Sasselov, 2017).

reactions.name: Ammonia addition to acrylonitrile

conditions.other: Anoxic aqueous ammonia; near-neutral to mildly alkaline conditions

reactions.mechanism: Ammonia adds across the activated alkene nitrile to give the beta-amino nitrile branch point.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) explicitly convert acrylonitrile to beta-aminopropionitrile by ammonia addition. No extra mineral assumption is needed here beyond aqueous ammonia availability, so the simplest chemically justified encoding is a direct solution-phase addition.

reactions.name: Cu-free H2S/UV reduction of beta-aminopropionitrile to beta-aminopropionaldehyde

conditions.other: UV irradiation; HS-/H2S photoreduction; staged after aminonitrile formation; anoxic

reactions.mechanism: Sulfide-enabled photoreductive partial hydrolysis converts the nitrile to the corresponding aldehyde with sulfur oxidation.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) show H2S/UV conversion of beta-aminopropionitrile to beta-aminopropionaldehyde. This Cu-free variant is retained because the broader cyanosulfidic system can use sulfide photochemistry without requiring copper at every step, although realistic sulfidic anion availability remains a geochemical constraint (Patel et al., 2015; Ranjan et al., 2018).

reactions.name: Cu-assisted H2S/UV reduction of beta-aminopropionitrile to beta-aminopropionaldehyde

conditions.other: UV irradiation; HS-/H2S present; copper-enabled photoredox cycling; anoxic

reactions.mechanism: The same sulfide-driven nitrile-to-aldehyde conversion is accelerated by Cu(I)/Cu(II) photoredox mediation.
reactions.reasoning: Copper photoredox accelerates several UV-driven reductions in the cyanosulfidic network, so a Cu-assisted version is chemically justified as an alternative to the slower Cu-free branch (Patel et al., 2015). The same surface constraints on UV availability and sulfur supply apply (Ranjan et al., 2018).

reactions.name: Cyanamide trapping of beta-aminopropionaldehyde to 3-guanidinopropanal

conditions.other: Freshly generated amino aldehyde intercepted by residual cyanamide; concentrated pool or wet-dry pulse; anoxic

reactions.mechanism: The terminal amine of the amino aldehyde reacts with cyanamide to install the guanidino functionality at the aldehyde stage.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) specifically found aldehyde-stage cyanamide trapping to be more effective than direct guanidination of beta-aminopropionitrile, making this the best-supported branch toward arginine. Cyanamide persistence in water is chemically plausible on prebiotic timescales even though it also participates in competing reactions (Patel et al., 2015; Steinman et al., 1964).

reactions.name: Cu-free cyanosulfidic homologation of the guanidinated C3 aldehyde to arginine alpha-aminonitrile

conditions.other: Net node represents staged use of two cyanide and two sulfide equivalents across cyanohydrin and thioamide chemistry; UV irradiation; anoxic

reactions.mechanism: Net Patel-style sequence of cyanohydrin formation, thioamide generation, UV-driven deoxygenation/reduction, and further homologation to the C5 alpha-aminonitrile precursor.
reactions.reasoning: This node compresses the experimentally supported Patel arginine branch from the guanidinated C3 aldehyde through cyanohydrin and thioamide intermediates to the arginine alpha-aminonitrile precursor, which Patel et al. (2015) explicitly characterize. The Cu-free variant reflects a slower but chemically defensible HS-/UV route; the literature still lacks an end-to-end environmental mass balance to free arginine itself (Patel et al., 2015; Ranjan et al., 2018).

reactions.name: Cu-assisted cyanosulfidic homologation of the guanidinated C3 aldehyde to arginine alpha-aminonitrile

conditions.other: Net node represents staged use of two cyanide and two sulfide equivalents; UV irradiation; copper-assisted photoredox; anoxic

reactions.mechanism: Copper-accelerated version of the Patel homologation sequence converts the guanidinated C3 aldehyde into the arginine alpha-aminonitrile precursor.
reactions.reasoning: Patel et al. (2015) show that Cu photoredox can accelerate related cyanosulfidic reductions, so a Cu-assisted homologation branch is chemically justified. The secure experimental endpoint remains the alpha-aminonitrile precursor rather than isolated free arginine, so this reaction is strong for precursor formation but not a full free-Arg demonstration (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Surface hydrolysis of arginine alpha-aminonitrile to arginine

conditions.other: Warm hydration during geothermal or evaporative cycling; prolonged contact with water; anoxic

reactions.mechanism: Sequential nitrile hydration and hydrolysis convert the alpha-aminonitrile to the amino acid with ammonia release.
reactions.reasoning: Hydrolysis of an alpha-aminonitrile to the amino acid is the expected Strecker endpoint, so arginine formation from the Patel precursor is chemically reasonable. However, Patel et al. (2015) do not quantify free arginine as the endpoint, so this surface hydrolysis step is chemically plausible but still partly speculative for Arg specifically.

reactions.name: Compartmental hydrolysis of arginine alpha-aminonitrile to arginine

conditions.other: Concentrated prebiotic pool, vesicle lumen, or mineral-confined compartment with heating-cooling cycles; anoxic

reactions.mechanism: The same nitrile-to-amino-acid hydrolysis occurs after concentration in a confined aqueous microenvironment.
reactions.reasoning: A concentrated prebiotic pool or compartment provides an alternative hydrolytic environment for the same aminonitrile-to-amino-acid conversion. This is again chemically reasonable but not directly measured as the terminating step of the Patel arginine branch, so it is retained as a lower-confidence endpoint (Patel et al., 2015).

reactions.name: Speculative cyanosulfidic homologation of beta-aminopropionaldehyde to ornithine

conditions.other: Net node represents staged use of two cyanide and two sulfide equivalents; wet-dry or flow-through cycling; anoxic

reactions.mechanism: By analogy to cyanosulfidic homologation, the C3 amino aldehyde undergoes iterative cyanide-based chain extension and reduction-hydrolysis to a C5 diamino acid skeleton.
reactions.reasoning: Speculative. No supplied study demonstrates beta-aminopropionaldehyde to ornithine under one prebiotic protocol. It is included because Patel et al. (2015) establish iterative HCN/H2S-based C-chain extension logic from related C3 nodes, while independent abiotic ornithine occurrence is supported in volcanic-discharge material (Johnson et al., 2008). This edge should be treated as a plausible bridge, not an experimentally established route.

reactions.name: Aqueous guanidination of ornithine by cyanamide to arginine

conditions.other: Concentrated aqueous pool or compartment; mildly alkaline to neutral; anoxic

reactions.mechanism: The terminal delta-amine of ornithine attacks cyanamide, and proton transfer-tautomerization installs the guanidino group of arginine.
reactions.reasoning: The late-stage chemistry is strong: cyanamide is a simple plausible guanidinating reagent (Steinman et al., 1964), and Longo et al. (2020) showed complete aqueous Orn-to-Arg conversion for ornithine residues in model peptides. The key caveat is context: the strongest evidence is peptide-bound rather than a fully naturalistic free-monomer pond simulation, so environmental free-arginine yield remains unresolved.

pathway_evaluations.feedback: Strong surface-only Patel-like route and well aligned with the literature up to arginine alpha-aminonitrile. Weak points are rxn_005, which likely stands for a cyanamide-trapped aldehyde or hemiaminal rather than a simple free aldehyde, rxn_006, which compresses several HCN/H2S/UV homologation steps into one edge and should explicitly use 2 mol_001 and 2 mol_006, and rxn_008, whose hydrolysis to free arginine is plausible but still weakly supported under generic surface conditions.
suggestions: Split rxn_006 into explicit cyanohydrin, alpha-hydroxythioamide, thioamide, photoreduction, and final amination substeps.
Represent mol_011 as a trapped guanidinated aldehyde or hemiaminal equivalent, or justify the simplified aldehyde node.
Specify hydrolysis conditions for rxn_008 or stop the high-confidence route at mol_012.
Add explicit coefficients: rxn_006 needs 2 mol_001 + 2 mol_006; rxn_008 needs 2 mol_007.

evaluation.network_feedback: Graph is connected, IDs are consistent, and the RDKit check reports no atom and charge conservation failures. Literature alignment is strong: the network correctly centers Patel's surficial cyanosulfidic chemistry as the best-supported de novo route, treats arginine alpha-aminonitrile as the most secure Arg-specific product, downgrades hydrolysis to free arginine, and marks the Orn-first branch speculative instead of overclaiming contested direct Arg reports or incomplete H2/Ni chemistry. The main weakness is coarse chemical granularity: rxn_005 oversimplifies the cyanamide-trapped aldehyde, rxn_006 and rxn_007 collapse a multistep HCN/H2S/UV/thioamide sequence, and rxn_008 and rxn_009 leave the crucial final hydrolysis underdefined. Add explicit coefficients to the balanceable reactions: rxn_006 and rxn_007 need 2 mol_001 + 2 mol_006, rxn_008 and rxn_009 need 2 mol_007, and rxn_010 needs 2 mol_001 + mol_007 + 2 mol_006. As a network to mol_012 it is good; as a network to free mol_014 it remains below approval, with P7 the strongest path and any biochemical compartment branch needing explicit transport and condition justification.
